description: Minimal: def main(), do: dbg(<<"x", digit(1)>>); @spec digit(integer) :: integer; defp digit(n), do: 48 + n. Interp and JIT both abort in runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs fz_bs_write_field_ref with "integer bit field expects Int"; the .99 AOT fixture shows the same failure. Controls: <<digit(1)>> and <<digit(1), digit(2)>> both succeed, so a direct call is valid until a preceding binary-literal segment shifts the dynamic field carrier. Expected output is "x1". This is distinct from fz-5xp.66, whose closure call fails even as the first field and whose ticket explicitly records direct calls as working. Add a three-door behavioral fixture and repair the construction field/value alignment rather than accepting a runtime tag panic.

comments.text: Implemented in e820bbee1. The ticket's carrier-shift hypothesis was disproved by the canonical backend signal: digit/1 still returned and bound an integer, but the preceding unsuffixed "x" field was emitted as Integer while its settled value/carrier was binary. Constant-only bitstrings had hidden the bug by folding before runtime construction. The final quoted-source decoder now reifies a raw binary literal field as BitType::Binary and shares the binary-literal spec authority already used by patterns; construction consumes the whole source binary, while patterns retain their byte-length boundary. Backend and all runtime doors remain consumers, with no compensating special case. Added a decoded-surface unit pin, a three-door behavioral fixture with controls and one/multiple preceding literals, and semantic-authority documentation. Proven red on interp/run/build and in the decoded-surface test before implementation. Final green: canonical backend fields Binary/Integer, full fixture matrix 715/715, compiler library 2019 passed/6 known ignored, runtime 260/260, CLI 30/30, doctests, AOT integration, clippy -D warnings, fmt, diff check, and commit hook. Supporting PR #136 was green before this commit/push boundary. Adjacent literal-string size-modifier validation was board-checked and recorded separately as fz-5xp.107.

title: A binary-literal bitstring segment shifts a following call result into the wrong carrier
